/pages/keywords/emergency-lighting-insta.h2: Planning an emergency lighting installation in Rochdale
paras: Rochdale has a wide spread of buildings that need escape lighting: converted mills split into units, terraced HMOs, shops on Yorkshire Street and the Wheatsheaf area, and newer blocks of flats near the town centre. Each of those needs a different layout, so an installation here starts with a walk of the escape routes rather than a fitting count taken from a drawing.

The survey records every route a person would use to leave the building, the stair cores, changes of direction, final exits, fire alarm call points and firefighting equipment. Those points set where luminaires and exit signs go. Open areas larger than the BS 5266 threshold get anti-panic lighting, and plant rooms or lift motor rooms get standby cover where the building needs it.

We then agree the type of system with you. Self-contained fittings with their own batteries suit most small blocks and shops in Rochdale because they need no central battery room. Larger mixed sites sometimes suit a central battery system, and some clients prefer self-test fittings so the monthly function test is logged without a person walking every corridor. We set out the trade-offs in the written quote so you can choose.

On site the work is planned around occupied buildings. Circuits are taken from the local lighting circuit so the fitting sees a mains failure on that area, wiring is fire-rated where the design calls for it, and each fitting is labelled. Once fitted, every luminaire is given a full rated-duration discharge test, usually three hours, before the paperwork is issued.

You receive a completion certificate, a marked-up plan showing each fitting, the test results and a logbook for the monthly checks. If an older system is already in place we can survey it first and tell you which fittings can stay, which need new batteries and which areas have no cover at all, so you only pay for what the building needs. Pricing is a written quote after the survey.
faqs: What does BS 5266 require for a building in Rochdale?

BS 5266-1 sets out where escape lighting is needed, how bright it must be on the escape route and how long it must run after a mains failure. In most rented and commercial buildings that means lighting along escape routes, at exits and stairs, and over safety equipment, with a three-hour duration in premises that may be reoccupied.
How often must emergency lighting be tested after installation?
A short functional test each month and a full rated-duration test once a year. The results go in the logbook we leave with you, and we can carry out the annual test for you if you prefer.
What does the installation certificate include?

The certificate covers the design, the installation and the commissioning test, with a plan of the fittings and the discharge test results, so the responsible person has a record for the fire risk assessment.
How long does an installation take in a small block?
A small block of flats with one stair core is often fitted in a day or two, depending on access and the wiring route. The survey confirms the time before work starts.

/pages/keywords/eicr/waddington.h2: Booking an EICR for a property in Waddington
paras: Waddington is a small Ribble Valley village near Clitheroe, with stone cottages, a few converted farm buildings and a handful of shops and holiday lets. Many of those properties have older wiring that has been altered over the years, which is exactly what an Electrical Installation Condition Report is designed to pick up.

An EICR is an inspection and test of the fixed wiring: the consumer unit, circuits, sockets, light fittings, earthing and bonding. The electrician samples circuits, tests insulation resistance, earth fault loop impedance and RCD operation, and checks for damage, overheating and wear. Portable appliances are not part of an EICR.

The report gives each observation a code. C1 means danger present and needs action straight away. C2 means potentially dangerous and must be put right. C3 means improvement recommended. FI means further investigation is needed. A report with any C1, C2 or FI is unsatisfactory, and we tell you plainly what the remedial work involves and quote for it separately.

For private landlords, the regulations require an EICR at least every five years and a copy for each tenant within 28 days of the inspection. Holiday lets and commercial premises in Waddington are usually inspected on a similar cycle, guided by insurers and the type of use. We email the certificate as a PDF so it can be passed straight to tenants or your letting agent.

Pricing starts from £160 for a typical small property, with a free written quote before work so larger houses or extra circuits are agreed in advance. Access is arranged with you or the tenant, and power is off only for short periods while each circuit is tested.
faqs: What does an EICR cover?
The fixed electrical installation: consumer unit, circuits, sockets, switches, light fittings, earthing and bonding. It does not cover portable appliances, which are a separate PAT test.
How long does an EICR take for a flat?
A one or two bedroom flat usually takes two to four hours, depending on the number of circuits and how easy the consumer unit is to reach.
When does a landlord need a new EICR?
At least every five years, or sooner if the previous report says so. Tenants must get a copy within 28 days of the inspection, and new tenants before they move in.
What do C1, C2 and C3 mean?
C1 is danger present, C2 is potentially dangerous, and C3 is an improvement recommended. C1 and C2 make the report unsatisfactory until remedial work is done and confirmed.

paras: EICR testing in Waddington covers village houses, barn conversions, the school and community buildings, and small commercial units along the road to Clitheroe. The test method is the same in each, but the time taken varies with the age of the wiring and how many circuits there are.

Testing starts with a visual check with the power on: the condition of the consumer unit, signs of heat damage, missing covers, cable routes and the main earthing and bonding to gas and water pipes. The installation is then isolated circuit by circuit for dead tests, which include continuity of protective conductors, ring circuit continuity and insulation resistance between conductors.

With power restored, live tests measure earth fault loop impedance and prospective fault current, and every RCD is tripped with a test instrument to check it disconnects within the required time. Results are entered on the schedule of test results so the next electrician can compare readings over time.

In older stone properties the most common findings are missing RCD protection, a lack of supplementary bonding in bathrooms, damaged accessories and earthing that does not meet current standards. Each finding is coded C1, C2, C3 or FI, and the summary page states whether the installation is satisfactory for continued use.

The report is usually written up and emailed within a couple of working days of the visit. Testing is from £160 for a typical small property, confirmed in a written quote before anyone attends. If remedial work is needed, it is quoted separately and a confirmation certificate is issued once it is done.
faqs: What tests are carried out during EICR testing?
Continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, earth fault loop impedance, prospective fault current and RCD trip times, plus a visual inspection of the whole fixed installation.
How soon do I get the report?
The report is normally emailed within a couple of working days of the inspection, as a PDF you can forward to tenants or your agent.
Will the power be off all day?
No. Power is isolated one circuit at a time for the dead tests, so most of the property stays live for most of the visit.

paras: Burscough has a mix of buildings that need escape lighting designed rather than guessed: the industrial estate off Tollgate Road, Burscough Wharf's shops and cafes, care settings, and converted houses let as flats. Design is the drawn layout and schedule of fittings. Installation is fitting and wiring it to that design. The annual test is the yearly three-hour discharge test of the installed system.

Usually yes. New partitions, a change of use or extra exits can leave parts of the escape route without enough light, so the layout should be reviewed.

Yes. The drawing and schedule are written so any competent electrician can install to them, and we can commission and test afterwards if you want.
